title: Optimal local prime chains contract from zero to the prescribed maximal ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative integral domain (so $ab=0$ implies $a=0$ or $b=0$), let $\mathfrak m\subset A$ be a maximal ideal, and let $B=A_{\mathfrak m}$ with canonical fraction map $\lambda:A\to B$, $a\mapsto a/1$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Suppose $r\geq0$ is an integer and $\dim A=\dim B=r$, with Krull dimension and strict prime chains as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $B$ has a strict prime chain $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_r$ of length $r$. For every such chain, its contracted ideals $\mathfrak p_i=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)$ are prime and satisfy $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_r\subseteq\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak p_0=(0)$, and $\mathfrak p_r=\mathfrak m$. Thus the contracted chain has both prescribed endpoints, including when $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization: prime extension and contraction; finite-supremum attainment and endpoint maximality expand the maximal-local-chain argument of Morphisms Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension, equality proof.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], every prime-chain length in $B$ is at most $r$, and their supremum is $r$. If $r>0$ and no chain had length $r$, all lengths, being integers, would be at most $r-1$, making that supremum at most $r-1$, a contradiction. If $r=0$, absence of a length-zero chain would mean there are no primes and hence dimension $-\infty$, again a contradiction. Thus a length-$r$ chain exists. Fix any such chain for the remaining steps. The same definition and $\dim A=r$ imply that every prime chain in $A$ has length at most $r$; we use this bound for both endpoints.

source.place: Tag 00KE, definition-Krull: dimension is the supremum of nonnegative integer prime-chain lengths; the finite-supremum attainment argument is written out here.

proof.text: The maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is prime: if $ab\in\mathfrak m$ and $a\notin\mathfrak m$, maximality gives $1=x+ca$ with $x\in\mathfrak m$, so $b=xb+cab\in\mathfrak m$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] to $R=A$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$. Contraction sends each $\mathfrak q_i$ to the prime $\mathfrak p_i=\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and preserves inclusions. If adjacent contracted primes were equal, injectivity of the stated bijection would give $\mathfrak q_i=\mathfrak q_{i+1}$, contradicting strictness. Thus the contracted chain is strict.

source.place: Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization: contraction and inverse extension for localization at the complement of a prime.

proof.text: The zero ideal of $A$ is proper and prime because $A$ is a nonzero domain: $ab\in(0)$ implies $a=0$ or $b=0$. Since $(0)$ is contained in every ideal, if $\mathfrak p_0\ne(0)$ then $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p_0$. Prepending $(0)$ to the contracted chain therefore gives a strict prime chain of length $r+1$ in $A$. This contradicts $\dim A=r$ by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and the bound established in step 1. Hence $\mathfrak p_0=(0)$.

source.place: Tag 00KE, definition-Krull: no prime chain in A can have length r+1 when dim A=r; explicit endpoint argument expanding the local-chain use in Morphisms Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension, equality proof.

proof.text: We already know $\mathfrak p_r\subseteq\mathfrak m$, and $\mathfrak m$ is prime by step 2. If this inclusion were strict, appending $\mathfrak m$ would give a strict prime chain of length $r+1$ in $A$, contrary to [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and $\dim A=r$. Thus $\mathfrak p_r=\mathfrak m$. When $r=0$ the same prepend and append arguments apply to the single prime $\mathfrak p_0$, giving $(0)=\mathfrak p_0=\mathfrak m$ without excluding this case.
